def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline:
## Definition

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.
lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $m,c>0$. Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open set of future timelike vectors and let $f$ be a smooth vector field along the bundle projection $\mathcal V\to M$, with $f(p,V)\in T_pM$ and $g_p(V,f(p,V))=0$. For every initial datum $(p_0,U_0)\in\mathcal V$ satisfying $g_{p_0}(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$, there is a unique local curve $(x,U)$ through it satisfying $D_sx=U$ and $D_sU=f(x,U)/m$. The solution depends smoothly on its initial data and on any finite-dimensional parameters on which $f$ depends smoothly, on a common sufficiently short compact interval near the base datum. It remains on the future unit timelike shell. There is a unique maximal solution on an open interval, but this interval need not be all of $\mathbb R$.
thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization:
## Statement

Let $x:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve on a nonempty open interval $I$, with parameter $s$ and tangent $T=dx/ds$. Fix $c>0$, $s_0\in I$, and $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$, and define $\ell(s)=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}$ and $\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^s\ell(r)\,dr$. Then $\tau'(s)=\ell(s)/c>0$, so $\tau$ is an increasing $C^2$ coordinate on its open image $J=\tau(I)$. The tangent with respect to this parameter is $U=dx/d\tau=cT/\ell$ and satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$. This is a mathematical reparametrization result; by itself it does not identify $\tau$ with a physical clock reading.

post-rpm-test-clock-and-background.physical_scope: Adopted classical test-particle framework on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold; the curved-background clock reading convention extends the flat ideal-clock postulate and is not an empirical accuracy claim.

post-rpm-test-clock-and-background:
## Postulate

**Adopted convention.** On a prescribed background $(M,g,N)$ from [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]], an ideal clock carried along a future timelike test worldline $x$ records the proper-time parameter $\tau$ defined by $d\tau=c^{-1}\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds$. Thus elapsed reading between two ordered points is the integral of this positive density. The flat-spacetime specialization is inherited from [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; extending that convention to the curved prescribed background is a separate adoption of this framework.

When the parameter $s$ is measured in seconds, $x^0=ct$ is in metres, $c$ is in metres per second, and $\tau$ is in seconds. This is a model postulate, not a theorem or a reported measurement. It does not assert that a physical clock realizes the idealization exactly, that the background solves gravitational field equations, or that the test body affects the background.
lem-rpm-length-action-first-variation:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $a<b$, and $x:[a,b]\to M$ a $C^2$ future timelike curve. Put $T=dx/ds$, $\ell=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}>0$, and for a constant $m>0$ and $c>0$ define the length action $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\ell(s)\,ds$. Let $H(\epsilon,s)$ be a $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variation through future timelike curves for $\epsilon$ near $0$, with $H(0,s)=x(s)$ and variation field $J=\partial_\epsilon H|_0$. Then

$$\delta S=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}S[H(\epsilon,\cdot)]\right|_{0}=-mc\int_a^b g\!\left(J,D_s\!\left(\frac{T}{\ell}\right)\right)ds.$$

Consequently $x$ is stationary under all such variations exactly when $D_s(T/\ell)=0$, equivalently $D_\tau U=0$ for the proper-time parameter of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. For any orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\phi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ with $\phi'>0$ and $s=\phi(r)$, the integral and stationarity equation are unchanged. This is a local variational statement; it makes no claim about global proper-time maximality, and the square-root action is not defined for a nonzero null tangent.

post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Classical spinless structureless point test body of constant primitive mass m>0 on a prescribed smooth background; no self-field, radiation reaction, finite-size, quantum, or global-completeness claim.

post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

For a spinless, structureless massive test body of constant primitive mass $m>0$ on a prescribed background satisfying [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]], adopt the action

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds=-mc^2\int d\tau,$$

for future timelike curves, with fixed-endpoint stationary paths as the model's free trajectories. When $s$ is measured in seconds, $T$ has units metres per second; in SI units the action has units joule-seconds. The equality is the proper-time change of variable of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. This is an adopted model premise, not a consequence of the metric or clock postulate. It excludes self-gravity, radiation reaction, spin, finite-size structure, particle creation, and quantum effects; it does not assert empirical adequacy for any particular body.
lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalenc:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $x:[a,b]\to M$ be a $C^2$ curve with parameter $s$ and $T=dx/ds$, fix $c>0$, let $e(s)>0$ be smooth, and let $m\ge0$ be constant. Take independent $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of $x$ and smooth interior variations of $e$. For the action

$$S_e[x,e]=\frac12\int_a^b\!\left(e^{-1}g(T,T)-em^2c^2\right)ds,$$

independent fixed-endpoint variations in $x$ and interior variations in $e$ give

$$g(T,T)+e^2m^2c^2=0,\qquad D_s(T/e)=0.$$

On the future timelike massive branch $m>0$, this constraint uniquely gives $e=\ell/(mc)$, $T/e=mU$, and the action reduces to $-mc\int\ell ds$; in proper-time gauge $s=\tau$, $e=1/m$. On the nonzero future null branch $m=0$, $P:=T/e$ is nonzero future null and $D_sP=0$; if $d\lambda=e\,ds$, then $dx/d\lambda=P$ and $D_\lambda P=0$. There is no null proper-time gauge, and the scale of $P$ remains initial data. Under an orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $s=\phi(r)$ between the parameter intervals, with $T_r=\phi'T$ and $e_r=\phi'e$, the einbein action is invariant.

post-rpm-null-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Separate classical massless test-particle sector with nonzero future-null momentum; no proper-time parameter, no P=mU identification, and no claim of empirical realization.

post-rpm-null-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

Adopt a distinct massless test-particle sector on the prescribed background of [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]]. Its primitive action uses a positive einbein $e(s)$,

$$S_0[x,e]=\frac12\int e^{-1}g(T,T)\,ds,\qquad T=dx/ds,$$

and independent stationary variations in $x$ and $e$. The variational equations and their null branch follow from [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]: the constraint is $g(T,T)=0$, and the physical branch requires $T$ to be nonzero and future-directed. The associated momentum $P=T/e$ is nonzero future null; its positive scale is primitive initial data, not $mU$ for any $m=0$ substitution. Null curves have no proper-time parameter. With $s$ in seconds, $T$ in metres per second, and $e$ in kg$^{-1}$, the integral has units joule-seconds. Under an increasing $C^1$ reparametrization $s=s(r)$, the paired transformation is $T_r=s' T$ and $e_r=s' e$, which leaves the functional invariant by [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]; this is the formulation's gauge freedom. Neither the scale nor a clock reading is inferred from the ray image alone.

This is an adopted classical model formulation, not an empirical observation or a theorem. Its scope excludes mass generation, interactions, and quantum field effects.

def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer.physical_scope: Definitions of point-particle momentum and observer-relative energy in the adopted massive and null test sectors; no conservation or empirical claim.

def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer:
## Definition

Use the massive and null sectors as separately adopted in [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]]. For a massive body of constant mass $m>0$, its **mechanical four-momentum** is $P=mU$, where $U$ is its future unit tangent with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. In the null sector, the mechanical four-momentum is the separately specified nonzero future-null vector $P$ from the einbein formulation; no null proper time or $P=mU$ is defined.

At an event, for any observer $n$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], define the spatial momentum and observer energy by

$$q_n(P):=P+g(P,n)n\in n^\perp,\qquad E_n(P):=-c\,g(P,n).$$

The projection identity and positive-definiteness of $n^\perp$ are supplied by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. With SI units, $P$ has units kg m s$^{-1}$, $q_n$ has the same units, and $E_n$ has units joules. This definition is pointwise and does not assert conservation, positivity, or an energy interpretation for an arbitrary vector field that is not an observer.

pthm-rpm-free-massive-and-null-geodesics.physical_scope: Conditional model deduction for free spinless test bodies on a prescribed smooth background; local initial-value solutions only, with no geodesic completeness or empirical universality claim.

pthm-rpm-free-massive-and-null-geodesics:
## Statement

On a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, stationary paths of the adopted massive action of [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] satisfy $D_\tau U=0$ in proper-time parameter, with $P=mU$ and $m>0$ constant. In the separately adopted null sector of [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]], stationary einbein paths have a nonzero future-null momentum $P$ satisfying $D_\lambda P=0$ in an affine parameter $\lambda$ with $dx/d\lambda=P$. Through each allowed initial point and tangent, each equation has a unique local solution and a unique maximal solution on an open interval. Neither maximal interval is asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

post-rpm-prescribed-force-law.physical_scope: A selected smooth external force law for a named massive test body of constant mass on a prescribed background; orthogonality is a compatibility condition preserving the mass shell, not a universal force principle.

post-rpm-prescribed-force-law:
## Postulate

For a named massive test body with constant primitive mass $m>0$ and momentum $P=mU$ as defined in [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]], one may adopt a specified smooth force field $f(x,V)$ on an open neighborhood of the future unit timelike shell within the future timelike velocity cone and the equation

$$D_\tau P=f(x,U),\qquad g(U,f)=0.$$

The orthogonality condition is part of this model's compatibility assumptions: it preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ for constant $m$. It is not a law selecting a force for every particle or interaction. A local IVP follows only where the named force field is smooth, as in [[lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp]]. The force has SI units newtons when $\tau$ is in seconds and $P$ has units kg m s$^{-1}$. No empirical force measurements, universal coupling, or global existence are asserted.

pthm-rpm-killing-particle-charge.physical_scope: Conditional scalar balance for a test particle and a specified Killing field; energy interpretation only for a future unit time-translation field, with no global symmetry assumption.

pthm-rpm-killing-particle-charge:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a smooth Killing field on a region of the prescribed background. For a massive test body obeying the force postulate, with constant $m>0$, $P=mU$ and $D_\tau P=f$, the scalar $g(K,P)$ obeys

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(K,P)=g(K,f).$$

Thus it is constant when the body is free ($f=0$). For a free null geodesic with affine tangent momentum $P$, $g(K,P)$ is constant along its affine parameter as well. If $K$ is a future unit timelike observer field along the curve, then $-c\,g(K,P)$ has energy units and is the energy defined by that observer; for a general Killing field it is only a conserved scalar, not automatically an energy.

pthm-rpm-mass-shell-and-force-work.physical_scope: Conditional constant-mass mass-shell and observer-decomposition identities; coordinate work relation only in flat inertial charts; variable-mass formula is kinematic only.

pthm-rpm-mass-shell-and-force-work:
## Statement

For a massive body with constant $m>0$, $P=mU$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and the force law of [[post-rpm-prescribed-force-law]],

$$g(P,P)=-m^2c^2.$$

For every observer $n$ at the event, the energy and spatial momentum defined in [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]] satisfy

$$E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2g(q_n(P),q_n(P)),\qquad E_n(P)>0.$$

For a nonzero future-null $P$, $E_n(P)=c\sqrt{g(q_n(P),q_n(P))}$. In a flat inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $n=e_0$ and inertial chart $x^0=ct$ from [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], let $E=E_n(P)$, let $\mathbf p$ be the spatial coordinates of $q_n(P)$ in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, set $\mathbf v=d\mathbf x/dt$, and define $\mathbf F=d\mathbf p/dt$. Then $dE/dt=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v$ under the constant-mass force hypotheses. If $m(\tau)>0$ is $C^1$, $U$ is $C^1$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $P=m(\tau)U$, then the kinematic identity $g(U,D_\tau P)=-c^2\dot m$ holds; it specifies no variable-mass law.

ex-rpm-incomplete.physical_scope: Explicit Lorentzian model manifolds illustrating that local flatness does not imply global causal regularity or geodesic completeness; these are mathematical countermodels, not claims about nature.

ex-rpm-clock-reunion.physical_scope: Conditional ideal-clock calculation for two specified piecewise-inertial flat worldlines that reunite; it is a model prediction, not an experimental report.

ex-rpm-null-scale.physical_scope: Algebraic illustration of affine-parameter and momentum-scale freedom for a null test-particle ray; no scale is inferred from the unparameterized image.

ex-rpm-straight.physical_scope: Direct flat-space solution of the adopted free massive test-particle equation; the displayed trajectory and conserved quantities are model deductions, not reported observations.
